items.prose: A test has 50 questions in 10 minutes.
items.question: When is question 30 due, in minutes?

feedback.correct: 12 s a question: Q30 at 360 s, 6 minutes.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the pace, then multiply by 30.

byKey.count-rate: You divided 30 by 10. The pace is 5 questions a minute, so Q30 is at 6 minutes.
byKey.seconds: 360 is in seconds. In minutes it is 6.

explain.text: 600 s over 50 questions is 12 s each. Question 30 is due at $30 \times 12 = 360$ s, which is 6 minutes. Equally, 5 a minute reaches 30 at minute 6.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Write the gaps, then their changes.

byKey.same-gap: You added 9, the last gap, again. The gaps grow by 2, so the next is 11.

explain.text: The gaps 3, 5, 7, 9 grow by 2, so the next gap is 11 and the term is 38. These are the squares plus 2: $6^2 + 2 = 38$.

items.prose: An order to buy 4,800 shares at £2.15 is 65% filled.
items.question: How many shares are still to fill?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. 65% is done, so 35% is left.

byKey.filled: 3,120 is the 65% already filled. The question asks what is left.
byKey.price: £10,320 is the order’s value. The price is not in this line.

explain.text: 65% filled leaves 35% open. 10% of 4,800 is 480, so 35% is $3.5 \times 480 = 1680$. The £2.15 is in the words but not the line.

items.prose: A forward-only sitting scored +1 right and −1 wrong. You answered 71 questions, 13 of them wrong.
items.question: What is your net score?

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find the right count, then take off the wrong ones.

byKey.right-count: 58 is the number right. Each wrong answer takes off a mark: $58 - 13 = 45$.

explain.text: 71 answered with 13 wrong leaves 58 right. Net is $58 - 13 = 45$, or $2 \times 58 - 71 = 45$. That is below the reported 50 to 60.

items.prose: A test that allows skipping. 45 s are left, and the last questions would take you 6, 12, 5, 20, 7, 4 and 9 s.
items.question: What is the most you can answer?

feedback.correct: Skip the 20 s one: the other six take 43 s.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Keep the cheapest until the next would pass 45 s.

byKey.drop-12: You skipped the 12 s one too. With it the six take 43 s, inside 45.
byKey.all: All seven take 63 s, over the 45 s left.

explain.text: Sorted: 4, 5, 6, 7, 9, 12, 20. The first six take 43 s, and the 20 s one would make 63. So six, with 2 s to spare.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. The gaps double; look for a fixed step after doubling.

byKey.same-gap: You added the last gap, 24, again. The gaps double, so the next is 48.
byKey.doubled: Doubling misses the −1 in every step: $2 \times 4 = 8$, not 7.

explain.text: Each term is double the last, less 1. The gaps 3, 6, 12, 24 double too, so the next gap is 48. Both give $49 + 48 = 97$.

items.prose: £3,600 is deposited at 5% a year, simple interest.
items.question: What interest is due after 4 months, in pounds?

feedback.correct: £180 a year; 4 months is a third: £60.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Find a year’s interest, then take $\tfrac{4}{12}$ of it.

byKey.year: £180 is a full year. Four months is a third of that.
byKey.months-as-years: You multiplied by 4 as if it were years. Divide the months by 12.

explain.text: A year’s interest is $3600 \times 0.05 = 180$. Four months is $\tfrac{4}{12} = \tfrac13$ of a year, so £60. In one line: $\tfrac{3600 \times 5 \times 4}{1200} = 60$.

items.prose: A review lists three questions from your mock.
items.question: Which one is a method gap?

options.why: Wrong in 6 s or less is a slip: you knew the way and erred. Care fixes it.
Right but over 12 s is a time loss, not a method gap.

feedback.correct: Wrong after more than 6 s: a method gap.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. A method gap is wrong and slow.

byKey.q12: Wrong in 6 s or less is a slip: you knew the way and erred. Care fixes it.
byKey.q47: Right but over 12 s is a time loss, not a method gap.

explain.text: Q31 took 9 s and was still wrong, so the method was missing. Q12 was a fast slip and Q47 a slow right answer. Only the method gap needs a drill of its own.

feedback.generic: Not quite right. Split the odd and even places.

byKey.even-row: 70 continues the even places, 100, 90, 80. The 7th place is odd: 3, 6, 12, so 24.

explain.text: Odd places read 3, 6, 12 and even places 100, 90, 80. The 7th term is in the odd places, so it is 24.

items.prose: A flight leaves at 22:35 and takes 3 h 50 min.
items.question: When does it land?

options.why: You turned 85 minutes into 25 and dropped the hour. 01:35 plus 50 minutes passes 02:00.
The clock passes midnight: 26:25 is 02:25 on the next day.
85 minutes is 1 h 25. Carry the hour: 02:25.

feedback.correct: 22:35 plus 3 hours is 01:35; plus 50 minutes is 02:25.
feedback.generic: Not quite right. Add the hours, then the minutes, and carry past 60 and past midnight.

byKey.carry: You turned 85 minutes into 25 and dropped the hour. 01:35 plus 50 minutes passes 02:00.
byKey.wrap: The clock passes midnight: 26:25 is 02:25 on the next day.
byKey.raw: 85 minutes is 1 h 25. Carry the hour: 02:25.

explain.text: Three hours take 22:35 to 01:35, past midnight. Then $35 + 50 = 85$ minutes, which is 1 h 25. So the flight lands at 02:25.
